research_question: Which machine-learning methods have been applied to computer-aided retrosynthesis prediction in organic chemistry?
queries: graph neural network reaction template extraction

candidates.title: Graph neural networks for data-driven retrosynthesis planning
candidates.abstract: We present a graph neural network framework that learns retrosynthetic disconnections directly from reaction databases. On the USPTO-50k benchmark the model recovers the reported disconnection in 72 percent of test cases, and a downstream Monte Carlo tree search uses the learned policy to plan multi-step routes. The approach requires no hand-coded reaction templates.

candidates.title: A curated benchmark of solubility measurements for small organic molecules
candidates.abstract: We release a curated dataset of aqueous solubility measurements for 4200 small organic molecules, harmonized from four public sources with explicit uncertainty estimates. Baseline random forest and kernel ridge models are provided to support reproducible comparison. No reaction prediction or synthesis planning task is considered in this work.

candidates.title: Transformer models translate reactants into products for reaction outcome prediction
candidates.abstract: Treating reaction prediction as a machine translation problem, we train an attention-based transformer that maps SMILES strings of reactants and reagents to products. The model reaches 90 percent top-1 accuracy on a public benchmark and generalizes to stereochemically annotated reactions without explicit atom mapping.
